# Jewish Studies Minor
Source: https://academiccatalog.umd.edu/undergraduate/colleges-schools/arts-humanities/jewish-studies/jewish-studies-minor/
Source: https://jewishstudies.umd.edu/academic-programs/undergraduate/js-minor
Source: https://arhu.umd.edu/academics/undergraduate-studies/minors
Fetched: 2026-09-28

## Catalog requirements

15 credits are to be distributed as follows:
Course | Title | Credits
History | 3
Literature | 3
Thought, Religion, or Culture | 3
Electives | 6
Total Credits | 15
A minimum of 9 credits must be at the 3xx or 4xx-level.
All credits must be earned with a grade of "C-" or above.
An overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor is required for graduation.
A list of qualifying courses in each category is available from the Director of the Jewish Studies program.
Up to 3 credits of 1xx or 2xx-level Hebrew or Yiddish language study may be credited toward the minor. In exceptional cases, students may petition to have other languages included.
Restrictions
Students enrolled in the Jewish Studies Major are not eligible to enroll in the minor.
At least 6 credits of 3xx or 4xx-level credit must be taken at the University of Maryland.
No more than 6 credits may be taken at an institution other than Maryland.
In keeping with University policy, no more than 6 credits may also be applied to a major.

By exploring its history, literature, culture, philosophy and texts, students complete the minor with a broad knowledge of Jewish life.
The minor in Jewish Studies offers students an opportunity to understand the full range of Jewish experience over the past four millennia. By exploring its history, literature, culture, philosophy, and texts, students complete the minor with a broad knowledge of Jewish life.
Students can earn a minor in Jewish Studies by taking 15 credits (5 courses) of Jewish Studies courses. No more than 6 of these credits can be earned at an institution other than UMD; up to 6 of these credits can be double-counted with an undergraduate major; at least 9 of these credits must be upper-level, at least 6 of which must be taken at the University.
Minor Requirements
Note that lower-level courses are at the 100- and 200-levels and upper-level courses are at the 300- and 400-levels.
The 15 credits must be distributed in the following manner:
1 course in Jewish history;
1 course in Jewish literature;
1 course in Jewish thought, religion, or culture;
2 courses in Jewish Studies (only 3 credits of lower-level Hebrew or Yiddish may be counted toward the minor)

Undergraduate Studies
Minors are an excellent way for students to gain expertise in an area beyond the major. We encourage students to work with their advisors early to incorporate the minor into their Academic Plans.
Applications for all minors remain open until the minor is filled. Students will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. When you click on the “contact form” below and select the appropriate option on the form, your request will be marked with the date and time. Please keep in mind that any pre-requisites must be completed by the time of application. (Students applying to the Music Performance minor must successfully pass an audition and should contact the advisor through the form below as soon as possible.)
When a minor is listed as CLOSED, it is closed until October 1 in the fall semester or March 1 in the spring semester. You may check this site again at these times. When a minor is listed as WAITLIST, it is closed, but you may put yourself on a waitlist by clicking on "contact form" below and selecting the appropriate option.
